comment: Single source of truth for what a machine needs before Revia runs.
Tools/CheckRequirements.ps1 is the only consumer; the README links to it
rather than repeating the list, because a list repeated in prose drifts.
Adding a dependency means adding one entry here. Nothing else.
file            - path under the repo root exists, optionally >= minimumBytes
command         - name resolves on PATH, optionally matching minimumVersion
pythonModule    - the interpreter at 'interpreter' can import every module
settingsPath    - Config/settings.json key holds a path, and that path exists
settingsPath exists because the hard failures are not missing files, they are
settings that point at a file nobody downloaded. Hardcoding the filename here

tiers.title: Build toolchain
tiers.summary: Needed to compile Revia at all. Without Qt the build still succeeds but produces the CLI only.

tiers.title: Chat and planning
tiers.summary: The language model and its server. Required for chat, /plan, and anything that reasons.

tiers.title: Long-term memory
tiers.summary: Embeddings for semantic recall. Revia runs without it but only remembers the current session.

tiers.title: Vision
tiers.summary: Multimodal projector for screen understanding and /look. Must match the chat model exactly.

tiers.title: Listening
tiers.summary: whisper.cpp for microphone input. Without it Revia is text-in only.

tiers.title: Voice Studio
tiers.summary: Qwen3-TTS for designed character voices. Windows SAPI is the zero-setup fallback, so this is a quality upgrade, not a dependency.

tiers.title: Image generation
tiers.summary: Local diffusion for /imagine. Off by default in settings.json.

requirements.label: CMake 3.20 or newer
requirements.fix: Install CMake, or let .\Tools\InstallQt.ps1 provide Qt's bundled copy.

requirements.label: Ninja
requirements.why: The debug preset generates Ninja build files.
requirements.fix: Install Ninja, or let .\Tools\InstallQt.ps1 provide Qt's bundled copy.

requirements.label: MinGW g++ 13 (x86_64)
requirements.why: The Qt kit is mingw_64. An MSVC kit is ABI-incompatible with this build and will link but crash.

requirements.label: Qt 6.8 mingw_64 (Core, Gui, Widgets, Svg, SvgWidgets)
requirements.why: The desktop shell needs it. Missing Qt is a warning, not an error, so the build quietly produces the CLI only.

requirements.label: llama.cpp server
requirements.why: Hosts the chat model. Revia starts and health-checks it.

requirements.label: Chat model weights
requirements.why: Not downloaded automatically: it is multi-gigabyte and model choice is personal.
requirements.fix: .\Tools\DownloadChatModel.ps1   (or place your own GGUF and set llm.modelPath)

requirements.label: Nomic Embed Text v1.5
requirements.why: Turns memories into vectors so recall is semantic rather than keyword.

requirements.label: Multimodal projector (Q8)
requirements.why: Must be the projector built for the exact chat model. A mismatched projector loads and then produces nonsense.

requirements.label: Python launcher with 3.12 (64-bit)
requirements.why: InstallQwenTTS.ps1 builds its venv with 'py -3.12 -m venv'. The launcher existing is not enough; 3.12 itself must be installed. This is the step that fails most often, and it fails after the folder is created, which makes it look like the install half-worked.
requirements.fix: Install 64-bit Python 3.12 from python.org, then re-run .\Tools\InstallQwenTTS.ps1

requirements.label: Qwen3-TTS Python environment
requirements.why: Revia launches this exact interpreter to run Tools/qwen_tts_service.py. If it is missing, Create voice fails with a generic process error.

requirements.label: torch and qwen_tts importable
requirements.why: The venv can exist while pip failed partway. Importing is the only honest check.

requirements.label: Voice service script
requirements.why: Tracked in Git, listed so a wrong qwenServiceScript setting is caught here rather than at first use.
requirements.fix: Restore Tools/qwen_tts_service.py from Git, or fix speech.qwenServiceScript.

requirements.label: Image generation Python environment
requirements.why: Owned worker for /imagine. image.enabled is false by default, so this is opt-in.

requirements.label: torch and diffusers importable
requirements.why: Same reason as the voice environment: a venv that exists is not a venv that works.
